shared_elements: low-relief curvilinear carved motifs on rock surface
stylised head-like forms with eye rendered as a small circle or boss
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow, flowing curvilinear relief built from crescents, hooked arcs and small circular bosses read as eyes, and in both the motifs are repeated in near-mirrored pairs, which is a fairly specific shared vocabulary rather than a generic one. The biggest difference in content is that A's carvings are organised as body-marking laid symmetrically over a large anthropomorphic figure (head, shoulders, ringed girdle, banded lower body), whereas B shows the same kind of motifs scattered freely over an irregular rock face with no governing figure.
